message.content:
Below are two ways to create a **Google Cloud Compute Engine** instance that has an **NVIDIA RTX A6000** GPU and runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**:

| Method | What you’ll run | Where it lives |
|--------|-----------------|----------------|
| **gcloud CLI** | `gcloud compute instances create …` | Your terminal (requires the Cloud SDK) |
| **REST API** | `POST https://compute.googleapis.com/...` | Any HTTP client (curl, Postman, etc.) |

> **NOTE**  
> *Google Cloud does not use the term “EC2”; that’s AWS. In GCP the equivalent is a Compute Engine instance.*  
> *Make sure you have the **Compute Engine API** enabled for your project and that you have the **GPU quota** for the RTX A6000 in the zone you choose.*

---

## 1. Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# 1️⃣  Pick a zone that supports RTX A6000 GPUs
ZONE="us-central1-a"          # e.g. us-central1-a, us-east1-b, etc.

# 2️⃣  Pick a machine type that can host the GPU
#     (n1-standard-8 gives 8 vCPUs & 30 GB RAM – adjust as needed)
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8"

# 3️⃣  Pick a name for the instance
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"

# 4️⃣  Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \
  --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
  --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --boot-disk-size=200GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
  --maintenance-policy=TERMINATE \
  --restart-on-failure \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh   # optional: install drivers, etc.
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--zone` | The GCP zone where the instance will live. |
| `--machine-type` | CPU & RAM allocation. |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image. |
| `--boot-disk-size` & `--boot-disk-type` | SSD boot disk, 200 GB. |
| `--accelerator` | Adds one RTX A6000 GPU. |
| `--maintenance-policy=TERMINATE` | The VM will be terminated (not stopped) during maintenance. |
| `--restart-on-failure` | Auto‑restart if the VM crashes. |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Optional script to run at boot (e.g., install NVIDIA drivers). |

> **Tip**: If you need more GPUs, change `count=1` to the desired number (subject to quota).

---

## 2. Using the REST API (curl example)

```bash
# 1️⃣  Set variables
PROJECT="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"

# 2️⃣  Build the JSON body
cat <<EOF > instance.json
{
  "name": "$INSTANCE_NAME",
  "machineType": "zones/$ZONE/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 200,
        "diskType": "zones/$ZONE/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000",
      "acceleratorCount": 1
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": [
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535"
      }
    ]
  }
}
EOF

# 3️⃣  Make the authenticated request
# (Assumes you have a valid OAuth 2.0 access token in $ACCESS_TOKEN)
curl -X POST \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/instances" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json
```

### Authentication

- Use **OAuth 2.0** with the scope `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform`.  
- You can obtain a token via `gcloud auth application-default print-access-token` or by using a service account key.

### What the JSON contains

| Field | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `name` | Instance name. |
| `machineType` | Full URL to the machine type. |
| `disks` | Boot disk configuration (Ubuntu 20.04 LTS). |
| `networkInterfaces` | Default VPC network + external IP. |
| `accelerators` | RTX A6000 GPU. |
| `serviceAccounts` | Permissions for the instance. |
| `metadata` | Optional startup script (installs NVIDIA driver). |

---

## Quick Checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|----|------|
| ✅ | Compute Engine API enabled |
| ✅ | GPU quota for RTX A6000 in chosen zone |
| ✅ | `gcloud` SDK installed (if using CLI) |
| ✅ | OAuth 2.0 token or service account key (if using REST) |
| ✅ | Optional: startup script to install NVIDIA drivers |

Once the instance is created, you can SSH into it and verify the GPU:

```bash
ssh ubuntu@$INSTANCE_NAME
nvidia-smi
```

You should see the RTX A6000 listed with its driver version. Happy GPU computing!
